questions.prompt: What happens when you read a let variable before its declaration line inside the same block?
options: Throws a ReferenceError due to the Temporal Dead Zone
questions.explanation: let and const bindings exist in the TDZ until initialized, throwing ReferenceError on earlier access.

questions.prompt: What does typeof null evaluate to in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Due to a legacy engine representation preserved for web compatibility, typeof null === "object".

questions.prompt: What happens if you call greet() on line 1 when line 3 is const greet = () => "hi";?
options: Throws a TypeError: greet is not a function
questions.explanation: const bindings are in the Temporal Dead Zone before line 3 executes, throwing ReferenceError.

questions.prompt: What does const getObj = () => { value: 42 }; console.log(getObj()); print?
questions.explanation: Without parentheses around the braces, value: is parsed as a statement label inside a function body that returns undefined.

questions.prompt: What does this snippet print?

codeSnippet.code:
const s = new Set([1, 2, 2, NaN, NaN]);
console.log(s.size);

questions.explanation: Set uses SameValueZero equality, so duplicate 2 and duplicate NaN are both deduplicated, leaving {1, 2, NaN} (size 3).

questions.prompt: What does [10, 2, 1].sort() return in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Without a comparator callback, Array.prototype.sort converts numbers to strings and compares lexicographically.

questions.prompt: Which modern static method safely checks whether an object owns a property even if created via Object.create(null)?
questions.explanation: Object.hasOwn(obj, key) checks own properties directly without relying on Object.prototype.

questions.prompt: If a user clicks #btn inside #parent, in what order do the console logs appear?
questions.explanation: Events flow top-down in capture phase (P-cap), fire at target (Btn), then bubble bottom-up (P-bub).

questions.prompt: What does this loop print after 10ms?

questions.prompt: What does a closure capture from its outer scope?
options: Live references to outer variable bindings
Immutable deep copies of outer values
questions.explanation: Closures maintain live references to their enclosing lexical environment bindings.

questions.prompt: Which binding rule has the HIGHEST precedence for a regular JavaScript function?
questions.explanation: new overrides even .bind()—precedence is new > explicit > implicit > default.

questions.prompt: What does this Promise chain print?

questions.prompt: If a .catch() handler returns the string "fallback" without throwing, what state is the returned Promise in?
options: Still rejected with the original error
questions.explanation: Returning normally from .catch() recovers the error and fulfills the downstream Promise with that return value.

questions.prompt: What happens if you write try { return fetchBadUrl(); } catch (e) { handle(e); } WITHOUT await?
options: The catch block is bypassed and the rejection escapes to the caller
The catch block catches the network error normally

questions.prompt: What does Object.hasOwn(dev, "toString") return for a normal object literal const dev = { name: "Ada" }?
questions.explanation: Object.hasOwn checks only direct own properties, ignoring inherited prototype methods like toString.

questions.prompt: What happens if a subclass constructor references this.name = "A" before calling super()?
options: Sets name on the parent prototype
questions.explanation: In derived classes, this is uninitialized until super() executes and returns the instance.

options: None of it—execution starts suspended until the first g.next()

questions.prompt: What does this ES2023 immutable array snippet print?
questions.explanation: toSorted() leaves original array a untouched (a[0] is 3) and returns a new sorted array b (b[0] is 1).

questions.prompt: Which ES2023 method returns a new array with element at index 1 replaced, without mutating the original array?
questions.explanation: Array.prototype.with(index, value) returns a shallow copy with the specified index updated immutably.

questions.prompt: Which utility ensures a search API call runs ONLY after the user stops typing for 300ms?
questions.explanation: Debounce resets the 300ms timer on every keystroke and invokes the function once typing pauses.

questions.prompt: Which object key allows an unsafe recursive merge to pollute Object.prototype?
questions.explanation: Copying the "__proto__" key into a plain object without filtering mutates Object.prototype unless explicitly blocked.
